evidence.meaning: Both editable login inputs initially empty; no fixed username evidenced. Both form fields are required.
Request fields are runtime username and password. Vue input models trim strings; no hash, encryption, or base64 transform occurs in the inspected login call chain.
Login is POST to the local user/login endpoint.
The ordinary Axios object transform serializes JSON and sets Content-Type application/json;charset=utf-8. Excerpt is the object branch within transformRequest, which begins at the recorded offset.

After the response interceptor returns the JSON body, Vuex consumes body.data.Authorization, userrole, and FirstLogin. Wire success shape is source-derived; actual token format and auxiliary field types remain unknown until a legitimate login.
Session material is forwarded verbatim in the Authorization header when the store token exists. The client does not add a Bearer prefix.

Body code 200 returns the JSON body. Every other body code rejects. Body code 401 and HTTP status 401 explicitly clear Authorization and redirect to the login route. Wrong-password-specific code is not established by this source.
Optional logout is POST with no explicit data. Vuex then clears local session state. Logout was not executed during source discovery.
The admin UI checks elapsed inactivity on a click and invokes logout after 900000 milliseconds. This does not establish the server token lifetime.
